item.title: New York governor condemns handling of Cornell rape case
item.description:
“In what world,” New York Gov. Kathy Hochul asked on Friday , “would the police learn from a victim that she’d been literally gang raped while she was intoxicated by five men in a fraternity house and not elevate those allegations to the district attorney?” Hochul was speaking about the case of a former Cornell student who said she was raped by several members of the university’s Chi Phi fraternity in 2024. At the time, the district attorney filed no criminal charges. The case has rocked the nation and forced a renewed reckoning over how sexual assault is dealt with in higher education. While the district attorney has defended his handling of the case , many politicians and legal experts are now examining whether certain details of the alleged victim’s account were neglected, and prosecutors have reopened the case. item.title: The Cornell 7: Allegations spark fury over gang rape culture
item.description:
People may quash their own beliefs to fit in with what they think the group believes. Andrew Lichtenstein/Corbis News via Getty Images As an undergrad student decades ago, I attended a dorm presentation describing the importance of giving and receiving sexual consent. The workshop leaders explained that if your partner said “no” or “stop” but you proceeded to have sex anyway, it was considered rape. A high-profile athlete on campus raised his hand and said, in utter disbelief, “That can’t be right. By that definition, everyone I’ve ever had sex with I’ve raped.” I was horrified by his comment, but most students laughed. He clearly saw nothing wrong with the view he’d expressed, presumably believing it was widely shared. item.description:

The missile was launched from the Wonsan area at about 6.30am towards the East Sea – also known as the Sea of Japan – and flew more than 700km (434 miles), the South Korean military said. item.title: Supreme Court ready to tackle climate, immigration and gun rights. Here are 5 cases to watch
item.description:
The Supreme Court on Monday will hear arguments in a case that could determine the fate of state-court lawsuits nationwide seeking climate damages from oil giants. Why it matters: Billions and billions of dollars are at stake for the oil industry in dozens of cases brought by state and local governments. Governments face mounting costs from climate change that litigants link directly to the companies' products. The big picture: SCOTUS is considering whether federal law blocks damage claims under state laws for the effects of interstate and global emissions. State of play: It's specifically about litigation against Exxon and Suncor that the city and county of Boulder filed in 2018. But dozens of state-court cases are active in California, Connecticut, New York, Massachusetts and beyond. The cases aren't identical. item.title: Prison chief in Christa Pike case oversaw five ‘botched’ executions, lawyers say
item.description:
Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee has halted executions for the year after the state botched its planned execution of Christa Pike, the lone woman on Tennessee’s death row, late Wednesday night. She would have been the first woman executed in the state in over 200 years. Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital , the drug used for the lethal injection, The New York Times reports from Nashville. Her lawyers said in emergency legal filings that after two syringes of lethal drugs were administered, Pike did not lose consciousness and still had a heartbeat, and that she described a burning pain in her arm. She has since been hospitalized and her attorneys said on Thursday afternoon that she is in critical condition, per the Times. She is 50 years old. The execution had initially been delayed by appeals. A federal appeals court halted proceedings on Wednesday morning, but then the U.S. Supreme Court…

item.title: 2 Lawsuits Cast Further Doubt on the Claim That ICE Agent Jonathan Ross Killed Renée Good in Self-Defense
item.description:
Jonathan Ross, the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent who fatally shot Minneapolis protester Renée Good on January 7, was not in any danger when he fired three rounds into the Honda Pilot she was driving, according to a pair of federal lawsuits that her brother and widow filed on Thursday. Nor was he responding to a threat that Good posed to anyone else, say the plaintiffs, who allege that Ross violated the Fourth Amendment and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) policies by using deadly force in circumstances that did not justify it. Based on video recorded by witnesses, we already had reason to doubt the assertion that Good "weaponize[d] her vehicle" and "attempted to run a law enforcement officer over," as Kristi Noem, then the DHS secretary, averred the day after the shooting. item.title: Trump says 'some' munitions are low as Iran war grinds on
item.description:
The US dispatched another aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the Middle East , signaling a potential escalation in the Iran war. US President Donald Trump said in a recent interview that a resumption of military strikes was “ possible ,” after last month rejecting an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran, meanwhile, is preparing its own response to any American attacks , Reuters reported. Iran seems “determined not to respond symbolically to a symbolic move and instead to escalate in the ⁠hope of reestablishing deterrence,” one expert said. Oil surged 4% on the news : Crude flows out of the Gulf last month were almost back to prewar levels, but analysts cautioned that any recovery in overall supply was fragile. — Prashant Rao

item.title: The Cornell Rape Lawsuit Is Fueling a Deranged Social Media Mob
item.description:
The New York Times has shared new details about a 2024 accusation of gang sexual assault at Cornell University; they appear to strengthen District Attorney Matthew Van Houten's argument that there was not a compelling legal basis to bring charges against seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity. But try telling that to the social media mob, which is going to absurd lengths to identify and destroy the seven men, who now face a lawsuit from the alleged victim , known only as Jane Doe. They were named in the lawsuit, and their pictures have appeared everywhere in the media. Websites have been formed with the express purpose of naming and shaming them, and The Cornell Daily Sun 's editorial about the accusations begins by listing them . item.title: Greece returns remains of Czar Samuel to Bulgaria
item.description:
Greek PM hopes handover of Tsar Samuel will help persuade Britain to return Parthenon marbles The remains of medieval ruler Tsar Samuel will arrive in Bulgaria on Saturday amid great pomp and ceremony, after decades of negotiations with neighbouring Greece. The remains – discovered in a Greek border area 60 years ago – are to be flown to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, onboard a military aircraft to be received with full state honours, including a fighter jet escort, a 21-gun salute and a procession to the Church of St Sophia, where the public will be able to pay respects. item.title: Ethiopia’s government forces retake airport from Tigray rebels in Mekelle
item.description:
Rebels from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) in Ethiopia were abandoning their regional capital of Mekkele in the north of the country on Saturday, according to local reports. The TPLF has been fighting against federal forces and pro-government militias since September 23 and launching attacks into neighbouring states, raising fears of an all-out civil war similar to that of 2020-2022.
